column2: That splendour, for a moment filling all directions and sub-directions, was stilled in an instant by the god of gods' illusion.
Then I saw the blessed Sthanu, Maheshvara, standing on the bull, gentle, like fire without smoke, the supreme lord with lovely-limbed Parvati,
the blue-throated great soul, unattached, a treasure of splendours, eighteen-armed, Sthanu, adorned with every ornament,
the god wearing white garments, white garlands and unguents, white-bannered, unassailable, with a white sacred thread,
surrounded by divine attendants singing, dancing and leaping here and there, with prowess equal to his own,
with the young moon as crown, pale, like the risen autumn moon, lit by three eyes like three risen suns.
On the god's white-shining body shone a garland strung with golden lotuses, adorned with jewels.
I saw embodied weapons, made wholly of splendour, of Bhava of boundless might, Govinda.
His great soul's bow, shining like a thousand rainbows, famed as Pinaka, was a great serpent,
seven-headed, huge-bodied, sharp-fanged, fierce with venom, its great neck wrapped by the bowstring, standing in the form of a person.
The arrow was like the sun, bright as the fire of time: that terrible divine weapon, the great Pashupata,
without a second, indescribable, terrifying to all beings, sparkling, huge-bodied, as if emitting fire,
one-footed, great-fanged, with a thousand heads and bellies, a thousand arms, tongues and eyes, as if spitting fire,
which is superior, mighty-armed, to the Brahma, Narayana, Indra, Agni and Varuna weapons, the breaker of all arms,
with which long ago the three cities were burnt and reduced to ash in a moment by one arrow, Govinda, by Mahadeva in sport.
Hurled from Maheshvara's arm, it would burn the entire world, the three worlds with moving and unmoving, in half a wink, without doubt.
For whom nothing is unslayable in this world, even among Brahma, Vishnu and the gods: that I saw, dear one, a highest being in wonder.
Another secret supreme weapon, equal to it or greater, is the one famed in all worlds as the trident of the trident-bearer.
It could split the whole earth or dry the great ocean or draw in the whole world when hurled by the trident-bearer.
By it Yuvanashva's son Mandhata, a universal emperor of great splendour, conqueror of the three worlds, was slain long ago with his army,
of great strength and valour, with prowess equal to Shakra's, by the rakshasa Lavana here, Govinda, with it merely in his hand.
That trident of extremely sharp point, very terrible, causing horripilation, standing as if threatening, with its three prongs like a frowning brow,
smokeless but flaming, dark, like a risen sun of time, with snakes in hand, indescribable, like Death with noose in hand: that weapon I saw near Rudra, Govinda.
The sharp-edged axe given long ago to Rama by pleased Mahadeva, destroyer of kshatriyas, by which the emperor Kartavirya was slain in the great battle,
by which the earth was made free of kshatriyas twenty-one times by Jamadagni's son Rama of untroubled deeds, Govinda,
with blazing edge, terrible-faced, its tip wrapped with a snake, stood near the trident-bearer like the flame of blazing fire.
Countless are the divine weapons of that wise one; these have been told by me to you, sinless one, according to their importance.
On the god's right side Brahma, grandfather of the world, mounted a divine car yoked with swans, swift as mind.
On the left side Narayana stood, mounted on Vainateya, bearing conch, discus and mace.
Skanda, mounted on a peacock, stood near the goddess, holding a spear at his throat like a second fire.
In front of the god I see Nandin standing, holding fast the trident, like a second Shankara.
The Manus beginning with Svayambhuva, the sages beginning with Bhrigu, and the gods beginning with Shakra, all came forward.
Saluting the great soul and surrounding him on all sides, the gods then praised Mahadeva with various hymns.
Brahma then praised Bhava, reciting the Rathantara; Narayana sang the lord of gods with the Jyeshtha Sama; Shakra recited the Shatarudriya, the excellent supreme Brahman.
Brahma, Narayana and the king of gods Kaushika, the three great souls, shone like three fires.
In the midst of them the god, the blessed Shiva, shone like the sun freed from autumn cloud, with a halo; then I praised the god of good vows with this hymn.
Homage to the god of gods, homage to Mahadeva; to Shakra, of Shakra's form, wearing Shakra's dress.
Homage to you, thunderbolt-handed, tawny and red, ever bearing the Pinaka in hand, bearing sword and trident.
Homage to you of black garment, with black curled hair, with black antelope skin as upper robe, and others as eighth.
To the white-coloured, the white, wearing white garments, smeared with white ash, devoted to white deeds.
You are Brahma among all gods, Nilalohita among the Rudras, and the self of all beings; in Sankhya you are called the Person.
You are the bull among the pure, the partless Shiva among the yogis, the householder among the stages, Maheshvara among lords, Kubera among all yakshas, and Vishnu among sacrifices.
Of mountains the great Meru, of stars the moon, Vasishtha among sages, and among planets you are called the sun.
Of forest animals you are the lion, the supreme lord, and among domestic animals the bull, blessed and honoured by the world.
Of the Adityas you are Vishnu, of the Vasus fire, of birds Vainateya and of serpents Ananta.
Of the Vedas the Sama Veda, of the Yajus the Shatarudriya, of yogis Sanatkumara, and of Sankhyas Kapila.
You are Shakra among the Maruts, god, the king of dharma among the ancestors, the world of Brahma among worlds, and among goals you are called liberation.
Of oceans the Milk Ocean, of mountains the Himalaya, of classes you are the brahmana, of brahmanas the initiated twice-born; you are the beginning of the worlds, and Time the destroyer.
Whatever other being in the worlds is remembered as having greater splendour, all that is the blessed one alone: so my mind is resolved.
Homage to you, blessed god; homage to you, tender to devotees; homage to you, lord of yoga; homage to you, source of the universe.
Be gracious to me, a devotee, miserable and wretched, joined with lack of lordship; be my goal, eternal one.
Whatever offence I did through ignorance, supreme lord, lord of gods, forgive all that, since I am your devotee.
I was bewildered, lord of gods, by the change of your form, and so I did not give you guest-water and foot-water, lord of gods.
Thus having praised Ishana, I offered everything to him, foot-water and guest-water, with devotion, with joined palms.
Then an auspicious shower of flowers, joined with cool water and divine fragrance, fell on my head, dear one.
Then a divine drum was beaten by the god's servants, and a holy wind blew, pure-scented and pleasant.
Then Mahadeva, bull-bannered, with his wife, pleased, spoke to the gods there, as if rejoicing me then:
See, gods, the supreme divine devotion of the great-souled Upamanyu to me, standing with single-mindedness.
Thus addressed by the trident-bearer, Krishna, the gods all with joined palms bowed to the bull-bannered one and said:
Blessed one, god of gods, lord of the world, master of the universe, may the best of the twice-born gain from you the fruit of all desires.
Thus addressed by the gods headed by Brahma, the blessed Ishana Shankara, as if smiling, said to me:

Son Upamanyu, I am pleased; see me, best of sages; you are firm in devotion, brahmana sage, for you were tested by me.
mahabharata:13:14.176	By this very devotion I am exceedingly pleased with you; therefore today I give you all desires as you wish.
When Mahadeva had so spoken to me, lord, tears flowed from joy and my hair stood on end.
Then I said to the god in a voice choked with joy, going to my knees on the ground and bowing again and again:

Today I am born, god; today my austerity is fruitful, since Mahadeva himself stands before me, pleased.
mahabharata:13:14.180	Whom the gods, though worshipping, do not see, the god of boundless prowess, him I have seen; who is more fortunate than I?
mahabharata:13:14.181	Thus the learned meditate on the supreme eternal principle, known as the twenty-sixth, the imperishable beyond the beyond.
mahabharata:13:14.182	This is the blessed god, the beginning of all principles, imperishable, knower of the arrangement of all principles, lord of Pradhana and Purusha.
mahabharata:13:14.183	The lord who created Brahma, the source of the world, from his right side, and likewise Vishnu from the left side for the protection of the world; and when the end of the age has come, the lord created Rudra from his body.
mahabharata:13:14.184	That Rudra, withdrawing the whole world, moving and unmoving, becoming Time of great splendour, like the fire of dissolution.
mahabharata:13:14.185	This god Mahadeva, having created the world, moving and unmoving, at the end of the age takes away the memory of all and stays.
mahabharata:13:14.186	All-pervading, the self of all beings, the origin of the becoming of all beings, he stays always all-pervading, unseen by all gods.
mahabharata:13:14.187	If a boon is to be given to me, if my lord is pleased, let my devotion to you, Shankara, be always, and eternal.
mahabharata:13:14.188	I wish to know past, future and present, lord; by your grace, best of gods, may that be.
mahabharata:13:14.189	And may I eat milk and rice imperishably with my kinsmen, and may your nearness be always at my hermitage.
Thus addressed, the blessed one, honoured by the world, Maheshvara of great splendour, teacher of the moving and unmoving, the lord, said to me:

Be ageless and deathless, free of the sorrows of existence, of good conduct, rich in qualities, all-knowing, pleasing to see.
mahabharata:13:14.192	Let your youth be imperishable and your splendour like fire; the Milk Ocean and the sea, wherever you wish, sage,
mahabharata:13:14.193	there, as you wish, the presence of the treasury of milk will be yours; eat milk and rice joined with nectar.
mahabharata:13:14.194	With your kinsmen for an age, then you will come to me; and I will make my presence always at your hermitage, best of the twice-born.
mahabharata:13:14.195	Stay, child, as you wish; you ought to have longing; when remembered I shall always give you sight, brahmana.
Having said this, the blessed one, shining like ten million suns, my lord, having given the boon, vanished right there.
Thus the god of gods was seen by me in concentration, Krishna, and I obtained all that was said by him, the wise one.
Directly, Krishna, see the perfected ones standing here, sages, Vidyadharas, yakshas, gandharvas and apsarases.
See the lovely trees, always joined with flowers and fruits, joined with flowers of all seasons, with glossy leaves and fine branches; all this, mighty-armed, is joined with divine nature."
For one like you the meeting with the gods is praiseworthy: a friend of brahmanas, non-cruel, and full of faith. I shall give you a prayer by which you will see Shankara.
[Krishna said:] I said to him, "Brahmana, by your grace, great sage, I shall see the lord of the gods, crusher of the hosts of Diti's sons."
On the eighth day I was duly initiated by the brahmana, with staff, shaven head, kusha grass, bark garment, smeared with ghee and girdled.
For one month I lived on fruit, the second on water, the third and fourth the same, and the fifth on air.
Standing on one foot, arms raised, unwearied, I saw in the sky, Bharata, the splendour of a thousand suns.
In the midst of that splendour, son of Pandu, a cloud, its limbs bound with rainbows, with a garland of lightning for its window, like a heap of dark mountains, adorned with cranes,
on which stood the blessed one of great splendour with the goddess, with austerity, splendour and beauty, with his blazing wife.
There the blessed Maheshvara shone with the goddess, like the sun with the moon standing in a cloud.
Crowned, mace-bearing, trident-handed, in tiger skin, matted, staff in hand, bearing the Pinaka and the thunderbolt, sharp-fanged, with fine armlets and a snake as sacred thread,
bearing a divine garland of many colours on his breast, hanging to the ankles; I saw him like the moon in a halo with twilight at the end of the rains.
Surrounded on every side by the hosts of Pramathas, hard to look at, like the sun in autumn with a halo.
And the eleven Rudras, self-controlled, praised him, the bull-rider, doer of good deeds, with their deeds.
The Adityas, Vasus, Sadhyas, Vishvedevas and the Ashvins praised the universal god with hymns of all kinds.
The blessed Shatakratu and Vishnu, sons of Aditi, and Brahma recite the Rathantara Sama near Bhava.
Many lords of yoga, Brahmarishis with their sons, and divine sages, honour the giver of yoga, the father, the teacher.
Earth and sky, stars and planets, half-months, months, seasons, nights, years, moments,
hours, winks and the revolutions of ages, divine sciences, O king, and all the directions bow to him.
Sanatkumara, the Vedas and the Itihasas, Marichi, Angiras, Atri, Pulastya, Pulaha, Kratu,
the seven Manus, Soma, Atharvan and Brihaspati, Bhrigu, Daksha, Kashyapa, Vasishtha and Kashya,
the metres, initiation, sacrifices, fees, fire, oblation, and the materials used for sacrifice, embodied, Yudhishthira,
all the lords of creatures, rivers, serpents, mountains, all the mothers of the gods, the wives of the gods and the maidens.
Thousands, tens of thousands and hundreds of millions of sages bow to the calm lord; mountains, oceans and directions too.
Gandharvas and apsarases, skilled in song and instruments, singing with divine melody, praise the wonderful Bhava; Vidyadharas, Danavas, Guhyakas and Rakshasas too.
And all beings, moving and unmoving, great king, bow to the lord with speech, mind and deeds. The lord of the gods, Sharva, stood before me.
Seeing Ishana standing before me, Bharata, the world with Prajapati and Shakra looked at me.
I had no power then to look at Mahadeva; then the god said to me, "See, Krishna, and speak."
When the god was saluted with my head, the goddess Uma was pleased; then I praised Sthanu, praised by the gods led by Brahma:

Homage to you, eternal womb of all; sages call you the lord of Brahma; the good call you austerity, sattva, rajas and tamas, and truth.
mahabharata:13:15.31	You are Brahma and Rudra, Varuna, Agni, Manu, Bhava, Dhatri, Tvashtri and Vidhatri; you are the lord facing every side.
mahabharata:13:15.32	From you are born beings, moving and unmoving; you are the beginning of all beings, and you alone are the dissolution.
mahabharata:13:15.33	The objects of the senses and all of mind, the seven winds and fire, and the gods who live in heaven: sages say that you are beyond these for men.
mahabharata:13:15.34	The Vedas, sacrifices, Soma, fee, fire and oblation, and whatever is used in sacrifice, all that, blessed one, is you, without doubt.
mahabharata:13:15.35	What is offered, given, studied, vows and observances, modesty, fame, Shri, splendour, contentment and success are offerings to you.
mahabharata:13:15.36	Desire, anger, fear, greed, intoxication, stiffness, envy, mental and bodily sicknesses, blessed one, are your children.
mahabharata:13:15.37	Doing, change, dissolution, Pradhana, origin, the imperishable, the womb of the mind's activity, and eternal nature, the unmanifest purifier, lord, thousand-rayed, golden.
mahabharata:13:15.38	You are the beginning of all qualities, the support of life; the great self, intellect, Brahma, universal, Shambhu, self-existent.
mahabharata:13:15.39	Buddhi, prajna, knowledge, awareness, fame, steadiness and memory: by synonymous words you are known as the great self.
mahabharata:13:15.40	Knowing you, a learned brahmana does not go to delusion; you are the heart of all beings, the knower of the field, praised by sages.
mahabharata:13:15.41	You have hands and feet everywhere, eyes, heads and mouths everywhere, ears everywhere in the world; you stand covering everything.
mahabharata:13:15.42	You are the fruit, sharp-rayed, in actions such as the winking; you are the Person of radiance, set in the heart of all; Anima, Laghima, Prapti, Ishana, the imperishable light.
mahabharata:13:15.43	In you are established intellect, mind, and those worlds that have taken refuge, the meditators, ever in yoga, true to their vows, masters of their senses.
mahabharata:13:15.44	He who knows you as fixed, dwelling in the cave, the lord, the ancient Person of universal form, golden, the supreme goal of the wise, that wise man abides, having passed beyond understanding.
mahabharata:13:15.45	Knowing the seven subtle ones and you as having six limbs, from your embodiment, the wise one, standing in the rule of Pradhana, enters you alone.
When this had been said by me, Partha, to Bhava, destroyer of distress, the whole world, moving and unmoving, uttered a lion's roar.
The groups of brahmins, gods and asuras, nagas, pishachas, ancestors, birds, hosts of rakshasas, all hosts of beings and the great sages bowed.
On my head fell heaps of fragrant divine flowers, and a very pleasant wind blew.
Looking at the goddess Uma and me, the blessed one, the benefit of the world, looking at Shatakratu too, Shankara himself said to me:

We know, Krishna, your supreme devotion to us, slayer of foes; do what is good for yourself; my joy in you is highest.
mahabharata:13:15.51	Choose eight boons, Krishna; I shall give them to you, best one; say, tiger of the Yadavas, which you wish, even the very hard to get.
[Krishna said:] "Firmness in dharma, slaying enemies in battle, the foremost fame and supreme strength, love of yoga, your nearness, and a hundred hundreds of sons I choose."
Thus told by me, Shankara said, "So be it."
Then the mother of the world, the earth, purifier of all, Uma, composed, Sharvani, treasury of austerities, said to me:
A son named Samba has been given to you by the blessed one, sinless one; take also from me eight desired boons; I give them to you. Bowing my head, I said to her, son of Pandu:
Absence of anger toward brahmanas, favour from my father, a hundred sons and supreme enjoyment, affection in the family, favour from my mother, I choose peace and skill.
[The goddess said:] "So it shall be, with immortal power; I never speak falsely at any time. Sixteen thousand wives, and in them dearness and imperishability,
and I give you highest affection from your kinsmen, and desirable beauty of body; seven thousand hundred guests will eat daily in your house."
[Vasudeva said:] Having thus given me boons, the god and the goddess, Bharata, vanished in that moment with the host, elder brother of Bhima.

He saw Mahadeva and praised the lord with hymns: "You are the purifier of the pure, the goal of those who go, best of those with goals; the fiercest of splendours, the highest austerity of austerities.
Vishvavasu, Hiranyaksha, Puruhuta, saluted, great giver of good, lord, abundant, truth: homage to you.
Giver of extinction to ascetics who strive fearing birth and death, thousand-rayed, homage to you, refuge of happiness.
Brahma, Shatakratu, Vishnu, the Vishvedevas and the great sages do not know you in truth; how shall we know?
From you Time proceeds, and in you Time dissolves; you alone are called Time, Person and Brahman.
Three bodies of yours are remembered by sages of the gods who know the Puranas: the supreme person, the self, the elements, the divine, the world, knowledge, and the sacrifice are you alone.
Knowing you dwelling in the body of the self, hard to know even for the gods, the learned go free to the supreme state without ill.
Without your wish, lord, birth and death occur in many ways; you are the door of heaven and liberation, you hinder and you give.
You are liberation and heaven, you are desire and anger, you are sattva, rajas and tamas, you are below and above.
Brahma, Vishnu and Rudra, Skanda and Indra, Savitri, Yama, Varuna, Indu, Manu, Dhatri, Vidhatri, and lord of wealth are you.
Earth, wind, light and water, speech, intellect, understanding and mind, action, truth and untruth, being and non-being are you alone.
The senses and the objects of the senses, that which is beyond nature, fixed, the state beyond the universe and non-universe, the thinkable and unthinkable, are you alone.
That which is supreme Brahman and that which is the supreme state, the goal of Sankhya and yoga, that are you, without doubt.
Surely today we are fulfilled, surely we have reached the goal of the good, the goal that those of pure understanding by knowledge reach here.
Ah, we were fools for a long time, senseless, that we did not know the supreme god, eternal, whom the wise know.
He, the god who favours devotees, whom knowing one eats nectar, has been reached directly by me after many births.
The eternal secret of gods, asuras and men, Brahman hidden in the cave, hard to know even for the gods,
this blessed god, the maker of all, facing every side, the self of all, all-seeing, all-pervading, all-knowing,
maker of breath, bearer of breath, the breathing one, giver of breath, the goal of living beings, maker of bodies, bearer of bodies, the embodied one, enjoyer of bodies, the goal of the embodied,
for those devoted to the way of the self, meditators, knowers of the self, wishing no rebirth, the goal is this lord.
He is the giver of good and bad goals to all beings; he would ordain birth and death in all creatures.
He is the lord who gives success to sages who wish for success, and the lord who gives liberation to twice-born who wish for liberation.
Having created all worlds beginning with the earth and the dwellers of heaven, the god supports with his eight bodies and gives.
From him everything proceeds, in him everything is established, and in him it goes to dissolution; he alone is eternal.
He is the highest world of truth for those who desire truth, the final liberation of the freed, the isolation of those who speak of the self.
This lord is hidden in the cave by the perfected ones headed by Brahma, lest he be revealed to gods, asuras and men.
Gods, asuras and men do not know you, Bhava, in truth; they are bewildered and made to enter by this very desire in the heart.
And those who approach him by devotion, Bharata, to them alone he shows the self by the self, this heart-dweller.
Knowing whom there is no rebirth nor death, knowing whom there is no higher knowable to be known,
gaining whom one thinks no gain greater, one reaches the supreme attainment, subtle as breath, bringing the imperishable.
Whom Sankhyas, knowers of the truth of qualities, skilled in Sankhya texts, devoted to subtle knowledge, knowing are freed from bondage,
whom knowers of the Veda say is to be known, established in the Upanishads, whom those devoted to breath-control always enter and mutter,
this is the sun, said to be the door of the paths of the gods, and the moon is the door of the paths of the ancestors.
This is the varied course of time at the beginnings of years and ages, in being and non-being at that time, in the northern and southern courses.
Thus the Prajapati, having long worshipped with many hymns, chose as his son the one named Nilalohita.
Whom they praise with the Rik verses, in the system of the rite many Rik verses; whom Adhvaryus offer in sacrifice as threefold knowable with the Yajus,
whom Sama singers of pure understanding sing with the Saman; he is the supreme womb of sacrifice and is remembered as its lord.
Night and day are ear and eye, the fortnights and months head and arms, the seasons strength, austerity steadiness; the year is his secret parts, thighs and feet.
Death, Yama, Fire, Time, the swift destroyer; the supreme womb of time, and this is eternal Time.
Moon and sun with stars, with planets and with wind, the pole star, the seven sages and the seven worlds.
Pradhana, the Great, the unmanifest, with the special ones to the end, the modified, from Brahma down to a blade of grass, the beginning of beings, being and non-being.
The eight natures, and what is beyond the natures, the whole portion of this god which revolves.
This is the highest bliss, and that which is eternal; this is the goal of the dispassionate, this the supreme state of the good.
This is the untroubled state, this is eternal Brahman; this is the supreme meditation of knowers of the scriptures and Vedangas.
This is the supreme limit, this the supreme part, this the supreme success, this the supreme goal.
This is the supreme peace, this the highest cessation, gaining which the creators thought "we have done what was to be done."
This is contentment, this success, this the Veda, this the tradition; for the knowers devoted to the way of the self, this is the imperishable attainment.
The goal of sacrificers who desire sacrifice, with sacrifices of large fees, the goal divine to the gods, that goal are you, eternal.
The goal of those who practise mutterings, oblations, vows, hardships, restraints and death of the body, god, in Vairaja, that goal are you.
The goal of those who have renounced action and become dispassionate, in the abode of Brahma, that goal are you, eternal.
For those who wish no rebirth and abide in dispassion, and of the modified and dissolved, that goal are you, eternal.
For those devoted to knowledge and realisation, the indescribable, stainless goal of isolation, god, the highest goal are you.
These five goals are remembered as told in the Veda, scripture and Purana; they are gained by your grace and not otherwise, lord."
Thus Tandi by austerity and yoga praised the imperishable Ishana, and sang the supreme Brahman that the maker of the world sang long ago.
Brahma, Shatakratu, Vishnu, the Vishvedevas and the great sages do not know you: then Shiva, pleased, said to him:

You will be imperishable and unchanging, free of sorrow, glorious, joined with splendour and with divine knowledge.
mahabharata:13:16.69	Your son, best of the twice-born, will be a maker of aphorisms, approachable by sages, by my grace; there is no doubt.
[Brihaspati said:] "I will not sacrifice for you today; choose, mighty-armed, whom you wish here as officiant who will perform your sacrifice."
Seeing the king lean, pale and unlike himself, wearied by fasting, surrounded by skin and bone,
Then, O king, Krishna met gods and sages and Charanas, the foremost gandharvas, the best apsarases, Siddhas and Sadhyas, who honoured him bowing.
Then the king of the Kurus Yudhishthira went, surrounded by gods, accompanied by Dharma and praised by great sages.
